statements.t: “The GFORCE-1 results reinforce our view that targeting NEK7 at the top of the NLRP3 signaling cascade could address a broader set of disease drivers than targeting individual downstream cytokines.

Our planned Phase 2 studies in coronary artery disease (CAD), gout, and hidradenitis suppurativa, conditions with major unmet needs, are intended to deepen our understanding of the therapeutic potential of NEK7 degradation.

With the emergence of next-generation urate-lowering drugs and their propensity to induce flares in the first 6 to 12 months of use, we believe the need for a well-tolerated, non-immunosuppressive flare prevention treatment will only increase.
We expect initial data from our Phase 2 gout study in H2 2027.
We look forward to a data update from this Phase 2 study in 2027, as well as a final data update from our completed Phase 1/2 study of MRT-2359 in combination with enzalutamide by year-end.

With our balance sheet expected to support operations into 2029, we are well positioned to pursue these opportunities while maintaining a disciplined focus on generating clinical evidence and advancing our pipeline.”
The study will evaluate prevention of flare recurrence following management of acute flares, with initial data expected in H2 2027.
